🐛 Fix `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` parameters of `APIRouter`

This fixes the issue reported in this comment: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14851#issuecomment-3863896385

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI


def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)


app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])

    return {"ok": True}
```

The issue is that in `APIRouter.__init__`, the `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` attributes are set on `self` before calling `super().__init__`. Since `APIRouter` inherits from `starlette.routing.Router`, and Starlette's `Router` (or its ancestors) might be initializing or overriding these attributes during its own `__init__`, the values passed to `APIRouter` are lost.

Specifically, the provided issue description points out that `APIRouter.on_startup` is set before `super().__init__`, and then it's overridden. Moving the `super().__init__` call to the top of the `__init__` method (or at least before setting `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown`) will ensure that the FastAPI-specific event handlers are correctly preserved.

ROOT CAUSE: `APIRouter.__init__` sets `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` before calling `super().__init__`, causing them to be overwritten by the parent class constructor.
CHANGE: Move the `super().__init__` call before the assignments of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown`.
